name: Pee-so-tum, at the gathering of August 1812
head: peesotum
review_note: review_required: a Potawatomi person of the gathering at Chicago in August 1812, the eve of the battle in which the garrison and its families were attacked. The card states only what the named sources say, says where a story is Kinzie family tradition rather than a contemporary account, and stages no speech or ceremony.

present_on_scene_date.note: Each person's own card says how their presence on 14 August is known.

associated_with.note: No source places his lodge in the camp; the card is put at one of the camp's grounds on the creek (the 1812 camp records) so it can be found, a reconstructed choice (liberty L-1812-people-3461).

not_in_this_household.note: No source names his family or places his lodge in the camp.

persons.name: Pee-so-tum

present_on_scene_date.note: At the camp on the 15th with Wells's scalp (Mrs Helm via Wau-Bun). No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: Warrior. Potawatomi (band not stated). 15 and 16 August: Mrs Helm says he carried Wells's scalp and (hearsay) stabbed Wells; Kirkland doubts the circumstances. Afterwards: Unknown.

evidence.quote: Pee-so-tum, who held dangling in his hand a scalp, which by the black ribbon around the queue I recognized as that of Captain Wells
evidence.claim: Helped Mrs Helm to the wigwams
evidence.tier: Kinzie family tradition (Wau-Bun; pamphlet 1836/1844, book 1856; Quaife App. II judges its speeches and dialogue invented)

evidence.quote: Pee-so-tum may have killed and scalped Wells, but it surely was not under such circumstances as those above set forth.
evidence.tier: secondary history (1884-1913), cite as compiler's statement
